Years ago, MacBooks came with a slot that allowed you to secure the device to a table leg or similar object using a cable lock. This was most useful in coffee shops, when you wanted to go back to the counter to order another drink without carrying your computer around with you.

Those slots have long disappeared, but you can now buy adapters to add a cable lock to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro…

You have to be a pretty seasoned MacBook user to remember the built-in security slots on the side of MacBooks. Those slots were designed for T-shaped accessories that you insert into the slot and then rotate 90 degrees to lock into place. The most common design was a cable loop that could be threaded through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now brought this concept back, launching adapters that can be installed on the corner or edge of a MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece construction with screws to clamp securely onto the MacBook.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version in addition to the original MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It should be emphasised that these locks have always been very low-security devices, designed only to stop someone from grabbing your MacBook and walking away in the few seconds when you are not paying attention. I have used one in a smaller coffee shop before, where I could still see my table when I went to the counter to get another tea, but I would never leave my MacBook out of my sight relying solely on this kind of lock.

These adapters are not cheap at $70, and you still have to buy the cable lock itself separately. But if you happen to have one lying around in a drawer, you might think it is worth digging it out and putting it to use again.
